blocks.prompt: 10. Consider the function \(f: \mathbb{R}^{+} \to \mathbb{R}^{+}\) defined by \(f(x) = e^{-x}\). Show that \(f(x)\) is a bijective.
blocks.explanation:
Bijective ka matlab hai one-to-one BHI aur onto BHI, yani do cheezein check karni hain.
Diya kya hai? \(f(x) = e^{-x}\), domain aur co-domain dono \(\mathbb{R}^{+}\) (positive real numbers).
Rule kaunsa? \(e\) ko undo karne wala auzaar natural log hai: \(\ln(e^t) = t\) aur \(y > 0\) ke liye \(e^{\ln y} = y\).
Plan: one-to-one saabit karna; phir chhape hue domain \(\mathbb{R}^{+}\) par onto check karna; aakhir mein batana ke yeh daawa kab sach hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(f(x) = e^{-x}\), domain aur co-domain \(\mathbb{R}^{+}\).
Humein dekhna hai: kya \(f\) one-to-one aur onto hai.
Tareeqa: One-to-one ke liye \(f(x_1) = f(x_2)\) maan kar dono taraf \(\ln\) lenge. Onto ke liye \(e^{-x} = y\) ko \(x\) ke liye solve kar ke dekhenge ke yeh \(x\) domain mein hai ya nahi. Yeh aakhri baat hi is sawal ki asal chaabi hai.

One-to-one
\[e^{-x_1} = e^{-x_2}\]
\[-x_1 = -x_2 \Rightarrow x_1 = x_2\]
Kyun: Dono taraf natural log liya; \(\ln(e^t) = t\) hai, is liye powers barabar ho gayin. Phir \(-1\) se multiply kiya. Yaani \(f\) one-to-one hai, chahe domain \(\mathbb{R}^{+}\) ho ya \(\mathbb{R}\).

\(x > 0\) kaunse outputs deta hai?
\[x > 0 \Rightarrow e^{x} > 1\]
\[0 < e^{-x} = \dfrac{1}{e^{x}} < 1\]
Kyun: \(e^{-x}\) asal mein \(\frac{1}{e^x}\) hai. \(x\) positive ho to \(e^x\) 1 se bara hota hai (jaise \(e^1 \approx 2.72\)), aur 1 se bare number ka ulta (reciprocal) hamesha 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan hota hai. Is liye outputs sirf \((0, 1)\) mein hain, poore \(\mathbb{R}^{+}\) mein nahi.

Onto ke khilaf misaal (counter-example)
\[e^{-x} = 2 \Rightarrow x = -\ln 2\]
\[-\ln 2 \approx -0.693 \notin \mathbb{R}^{+}\]
Kyun: Output 2 co-domain \(\mathbb{R}^{+}\) mein hai. Us ke liye input \(-\ln 2\) chahiye jo negative hai, yani domain \(\mathbb{R}^{+}\) mein nahi. Is liye 2 ka koi pre-image nahi. Jaisa chhapa hai, \(f\) onto nahi, aur is liye bijective bhi nahi.
Dhyan dein: Bahut si guides is sawal ko bijective "saabit" kar deti hain, kyunke woh domain ko chupke se \(\mathbb{R}\) maan leti hain. Hamesha check karein ke nikala hua input waqai domain mein hai.

Sahi daawa: domain \(\mathbb{R}\)
\[y > 0:\; x = -\ln y \in \mathbb{R}\]
\[f(-\ln y) = e^{\ln y} = y \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Agar function \(f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^{+}\) ho, to har positive \(y\) ka input \(-\ln y\) mojood hai (log sirf positive numbers ka hota hai, aur \(y\) positive hai). Yeh input real hai, is liye \(f\) onto hai. One-to-one pehle hi saabit hai, is liye \(f\) bijective hai.

Graph se tasdeeq
Kyun: Graph dekhein: har horizontal line \(y = c\) (\(c > 0\)) poore curve ko bilkul ek dafa kaat'ti hai, yani \(\mathbb{R}\) par one-to-one aur onto. Lekin \(c \ge 1\) wali lines curve ko \(x \le 0\) par kaat'ti hain, jo chhape hue domain se bahar hai. Isi liye \(\mathbb{R}^{+}\) par onto nahi.
blocks.final_answer: Jaisa chhapa hai (\(f: \mathbb{R}^{+} \to \mathbb{R}^{+}\)), \(f\) one-to-one hai lekin onto nahi (range \((0, 1)\)), is liye bijective nahi. \(f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^{+}\), \(f(x) = e^{-x}\) bijective hai (\(y\) ka pre-image \(-\ln y\)).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab kehti hai ke \(f: \mathbb{R}^{+} \to \mathbb{R}^{+}\), \(f(x) = e^{-x}\) ko bijective saabit karein. Jaisa chhapa hai yeh daawa ghalat hai: \(x > 0\) par \(e^{-x}\) sirf \((0, 1)\) mein hota hai, is liye misaal ke taur par \(2 \in \mathbb{R}^{+}\) kabhi output nahi banta (agar \(\mathbb{R}^{+}\) mein 0 bhi shamil ho to range \((0, 1]\) banti hai, phir bhi poora \(\mathbb{R}^{+}\) nahi). Durust sawal \(f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^{+}\) hai, jo bijective hai (yeh bhi sahi hai: \(f: \mathbb{R}^{+} \to (0, 1)\)). Answer key mein is ka koi jawab nahi chhapa.
